In summary, our research is concerned with
the right to be/learn for young people in the EJA.
the question of how to understand the right to be/learn of young people who are enrolled in Adult and Youth Education.
the rights of young people in the Brazilian EJA (Educacao de Jovem e Adulto) and the ways they are exercised in the EJA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

EJA is a place for the rights of plural subjects, a place for the production of knowledge by the youth and other social subjects, a space of potentialities for the understanding of the EJA as a space of the production of knowledge of the plurality of the young people, convergent with the knowledge/skills of other people in other phases of life (adults and the elderly).
the EJA is a place of plural rights of subjects that compose it.

, in the EJA, it is possible to understand the youth as a social construction that is in constant process of being constructed and reconstructed, in which it is necessary to recognize that it is a plural and diverse group that has its specificities, which are not always recognized by society.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the EJA (Education for Youth and Adults) is a place constituted by the rights of the plural subjects who make up the EJA.
the young people in the EJA (Young People Education and Adults) have the right to be and to learn.
it is necessary to think the EJA as a place constituted by plural and different rights of the subjects that are part of it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the youth who participate in EJA are not only a social group with particularities, but are also a social group with a history of struggle for their rights.
the young people in EJA are not just students but also subjects of rights.

the EJA is a place where young people are entitled to be, and where they can develop their own knowledge and culture, and that the school should be a place where young and adult people can meet, and learn from each other.
